hints.title: Fix the sign of the input
hints.body: Analyse the recurrence for a fixed negative input and a fixed nonnegative input separately. Write the first few function expressions on each half-axis, applying the outer modulus after each update.
hints.recap: A modulus formula may behave differently on the two sides of zero.
hints.pitfall: Do not substitute a later index into a pattern before checking how the recurrence produces the next term.
hints.pause: Calculate the early expressions separately on each half-axis.

recall.reminder: Initial terms suggest a pattern, but the recurrence must justify why its update continues.

hints.title: Justify the update pattern
hints.body: On each half-axis, use your early expressions to identify the update rule that continues. Check whether the index affects which expression applies and explain why the same update argument can be repeated.
hints.recap: A repeated state gives a cycle only when the recurrence sends it to the same next state.
hints.pitfall: The two half-axes need not have the same kind of pattern.
hints.pause: Use the recurrence to justify your patterns and determine the two pieces of the requested function.

recall.reminder: A repeated state gives a cycle only when the recurrence sends it to the same next state.

hints.title: Accumulate the two pieces separately
hints.body: Split the integral at zero using your piecewise expression. Integrate the resulting simple pieces, or calculate their geometric areas where the function is nonnegative.
hints.recap: An integral across a formula change is the sum of the integrals on the separate intervals.
hints.pitfall: A large index does not mean a large power of the input; use the recurrence expression you derived.
hints.pause: Find each contribution and combine them to obtain the requested integral.

recall.reminder: An integral across a formula change is the sum of the integrals on the separate intervals.

solution:
1. Follow nonnegative inputs. If x≥0, the first function is f1(x)=x. Each recurrence update adds another x, and the result remains nonnegative, so fn(x)=nx.

2. Follow negative inputs. If x<0, then f1(x)=−x. The next value is |−x+x|=0, and the next is |0+x|=−x. These two states repeat under the recurrence: odd indices give −x and even indices give 0.

3. Select the requested index. Since 99 is odd, f99(x)=−x on [−1,0) and f99(x)=99x on [0,1]. Both pieces are zero at the joining point.

4. Integrate. The two contributions are ∫−10(−x)dx=12 and ∫0199xdx=992. Their sum is 50.

Answer E. Equivalently, add the areas of the two right triangles under the graph.
knowledgePattern: Analyse a function recurrence separately on two half-axes before integrating a distant term
